limitations: Significant field coverage gaps in legacy catalogs (Hipparcos, TIC, AllWISE) and literature sources, restricting direct multi-era comparisons
Proper motion values exhibit epoch-dependent dispersion due to differing observation baselines and lack of linear extrapolation in raw catalog entries
Systematic zero-point offsets (~0.05 mas) exist between Gaia and older optical/IR missions, complicating direct parallax/PM fusion
Literature extractions contain documented artifacts (e.g., sign convention mismatches, unit errors, outlier values) requiring manual curation
Direct distance inversion (d=1000/π) is only reliable for high signal-to-noise measurements; low-S/N or negative parallaxes must be excluded or treated statistically
recommended_caveats: Normalize all astrometric parameters to a common reference epoch (e.g., J2016.0) and apply cos(δ) projection corrections before cross-catalog matching
Apply mission-specific systematic corrections (e.g., Gaia zonal errors, Hipparcos re-reduction offsets) when combining parallax or proper motion datasets
Validate literature-derived values against modern Gaia DR3 baselines; discard records with σ(π)/π > 0.2 or unexplained sign/unit discrepancies
Account for potential binary orbital motion when analyzing long-term proper motion residuals, especially for high-precision kinematic modeling
When computing tangential velocities, explicitly propagate uncertainties from both parallax and proper motion rather than treating them as independent fixed values

overall_narrative: This analysis of ten astrometric parameters and their cross-relations confirms Proxima Centauri’s status as the nearest star to the Sun at ~1.3 pc, anchored by highly precise Gaia DR3 parallax measurements. The star’s exceptional kinematics are characterized by a total proper motion of ~3.86 arcseconds/year, driven by rapid westward and northward apparent shifts that modern space-based astrometry captures with minimal uncertainty. While legacy catalogs (e.g., Hipparcos, TIC) exhibit broader parameter dispersions due to lower precision and epoch misalignments, they reliably converge with Gaia-derived baselines through systematic cross-matching.
